question.problem:
Given the function  $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2\cdot {3}^{x}-1$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2\cdot {3}^{x}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+2\cdot {3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{1}{x}+2\cdot {3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3))|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}+2\cdot {3}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\  & =1+6\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)\,.\end{aligned}
$$
